newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares keep most gains to close at record.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares keep most gains to close at record.

text.p: Russian shares surged on Tuesday as Western demand prompted feverish local buying, traders said, offering mixed predictions for Wednesday's trade.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares hit a new record, rising 2.52 percent to 312.60 on $50.01 million volume for the entire market.
"Everyone was waiting for a correction today, but a big order came in and UES EESR.RTS rose, bringing up the whole market," said a UFG trader Maxim Perlin.
Traders said the rally would be shorter than January's three-week run and said the market had calmed down by Tuesday evening leaving volumes healthy but not high.
"We did not see much profit-taking, even among the blue chips, despite high levels," Perlin said. "Everyone it seems is sure the market will grow in 1997."
"I think the peak is over," said Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin, adding that local funds could not support the market and the foreign funds flow had slowed.
"It was a mind-game. I cannot understand why one should buy Rostelekom at four dollars, and UES at 21 cents."
UES closed at $0.2020, off a high of $0.2200 but up from $0.1955 at Monday's close. Rostelekom eased to $4.000 from $4.065.
Perlin said Irkutskenergo eased midday on news of its 1996 results and dragged down other shares by two percent. Irkutsenergo rose to $0.310 from $0.308.
But he said second-tier shares would show most future growth.
"Investors who have been here for a long time do not invest in blue chips," Perlin said. "Regional telecoms are hot and the discount of preferred shares to ordinaries will shrink."
LUKoil preferreds rose to $11.63 from $11.35 and Megionneftegaz prefs firmed to $4.55 from $4.35.
